anomalies.observed: On the Power sheet (power.kicad_sch, page 4/4) the fan headers are wired as pin1 = +12V, pin2 = FAN_0_TACH / FAN_1_TACH, pin3 = GND, pin4 = no-connect. The +12V rail is tapped to the TOP terminal (pin 1) of both J7 and J8, the tach signal to pin 2, and GND to pin 3.
anomalies.expected: The specification states the 12 V rail feeds 'the two fan-header 12 V pins (J7/J8 pin 2)', i.e. the standard 4-pin fan pinout (pin1 = GND, pin2 = +12V, pin3 = tach). The build shifts every power/sense pin by one position, so +12V lands on pin1 and the tach on pin2.

evidence.quote: Power sheet (4/4): J7/J8 Conn_01x04_Pin — pin 1 tied to +12V, pin 2 tied to FAN_0_TACH/FAN_1_TACH, pin 3 tied to GND, pin 4 marked NC (X)
Also on this net: ... and the two fan-header 12 V pins (J7/J8 pin 2).

anomalies.impact: A standard 4-pin cooling fan plugged into J7/J8 would receive +12 V on its ground wire and the 3.3 V-pulled tach signal on its +12 V wire, with GND on its tach pin. The fans would not spin, the tachometer inputs would not read correctly, and the fan's power pin could be back-driven/damaged. The firmware's fan-stall monitoring would be inoperative.

parsed.summary: The board otherwise matches the specification (power mux, buck, heater high-side switch, three MAX31855 channels, SPI/CS mapping, USB-C pulldowns, ILIM/SS passives all correct), but the fan headers J7/J8 are wired one pin-position off from the intended 12 V-on-pin-2 layout, miswiring the fan power, ground and tach lines.
